c.tagline: Alpine capital where a medieval old town meets the ski slopes.

taxi.fareNote: Uber availability is very limited in Innsbruck; most rides are booked by phone or app through local firms such as Taxi 5311. Fares are metered and there is no street-hailing culture.

emergency.note: 112 is the EU-wide emergency number; 133 reaches police and 144 the ambulance directly.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

hood_desc: The medieval Old Town, a compact maze of arcaded lanes crowned by the famous Golden Roof (Goldenes Dachl), packed with Tyrolean taverns, wine bars, and the Imperial Palace; the must-stay for first-timers who want the sights on their doorstep.

A calm, well-connected district just south of the centre around the main railway station and Wilten Basilica, with fast trains out to the ski resorts; a practical, good-value base for skiers and first-time visitors.
A hillside residential quarter on the sunny northern slopes with panoramic valley views and direct access to Nordkette hiking trails; suits walkers and those wanting a quiet, scenic perch above town.

An elegant, leafy villa quarter of Belle Époque houses near the Hofgarten and the river, one of Innsbruck's most refined and peaceful residential areas; good for a relaxed, upscale stay close to the centre.

A lively local residential neighbourhood just across the Sill river from the centre, with everyday shops, cafes, and parks and easy tram links; an affordable, authentic place to stay away from the tourist crush.

water.note: Alpine tap water is excellent and safe to drink.

transit.hours: Trams and buses run roughly 5am-11:30pm, with Nightliner buses on Friday and Saturday nights; the Nordkette cable cars and Hungerburgbahn run daytime hours only.
transit.note: The IVB network of trams and buses covers the city and valley, linked to the Nordkette mountain by the Hungerburgbahn funicular and the cable cars up to Hafelekar.
transit.pay: Buy single tickets (about €2.90) or a 24-hour ticket (about €5.90) from the IVB app, ticket machines, or Tabak-Trafik shops, and validate on board; the same tickets cover trams and buses. The Nordkette cable cars and Hungerburgbahn need separate mountain tickets, or ride free with the Innsbruck Card.

bus: Innsbruck Hauptbahnhof bus terminal (ÖBB Postbus / FlixBus)

transit.m: Line F bus to Hauptbahnhof and old town (~20 min, every 15 min)

tip.r: Rounding up or adding about 5-10% for good service is customary; tell the server the total amount when you pay rather than leaving coins on the table.

food.name: Tiroler Grostl
food.desc: Leftover roast beef or pork fried with potato, onion and caraway in a black iron pan, crowned with a fried egg - the Tyrolean mountain hangover cure.

places.name: Gasthaus Anich
places.note: Long-standing locals' meeting point near the shopping streets; unfussy Austrian comfort cooking done right.

places.name: Weisses Rossl
places.note: Tyrolean inn with roots in the 1500s; one of the most recommended places in town for regional classics.

places.name: Stiftskeller
places.note: Vaulted stone cellars and a big beer garden in the centre; reliable Grostl and goulash with Austrian beer.

food.name: Kasspatzln
food.desc: Ragged egg-noodle spaetzle layered with pungent mountain cheese and buried under sweet fried onions, served straight from the pan with a green salad.

places.name: Die Wilderin
places.note: Farm-to-table kitchen with a weekly-changing menu and a strong line in reworked Tyrolean classics.

places.name: Gasthaus Anich
places.note: Kasespatzle, schnitzel and roast pork with crackling; the everyday version locals actually eat.

places.name: Weisses Rossl
places.note: Wood-panelled rooms and a generous cheese-noodle pan that easily feeds two.

food.name: Tiroler Speck and Brettljause
food.desc: Cold-smoked, juniper-cured mountain bacon sliced thin onto a board with mountain cheese, kaminwurzen sausage, horseradish and dark bread.

places.name: Speckeria
places.note: Tiny Speck specialist by the Golden Roof; boards to eat in and vacuum-packed slabs to take home.

places.name: Markthalle Innsbruck
places.note: Covered market where butchers and cheesemongers assemble a jause to eat at the counter with a glass of wine.

places.name: Gasthof Riese Haymon
places.note: Generations-old inn away from the tourist streets, good for a full board plus dumpling specialities.

food.name: Knodel
food.desc: Bread dumplings bound with Speck, spinach or cheese, eaten in clear beef broth or sliced and pan-fried with sauerkraut and browned butter.

places.name: Gasthof Riese Haymon
places.note: Named for a Tyrolean giant and famous for its dumpling menu; a local dining room rather than a tourist stop.

places.name: Restaurant Ottoburg
places.note: Fourteenth-century tower house with vaulted rooms; classic Speckknodel and seasonal game.

places.name: Stiftskeller
places.note: Dumpling trio in broth is a good, cheap lunch before the mountain lifts.

food.name: Kaiserschmarrn
food.desc: Fluffy pancake torn into shreds in the pan, caramelised with sugar and raisins, dusted with icing sugar and served with plum compote - a main, not a side.

places.name: Gasthaus Anich
places.note: Properly fluffy Kaiserschmarrn made to order; expect a 20-minute wait and a plate for two.

places.name: Restaurant Ottoburg
places.note: Atmospheric medieval rooms and a classic version with Zwetschkenroster plum compote.

places.name: Weisses Rossl
places.note: Traditional inn finish to a Tyrolean dinner, big enough to share three ways.

food.name: Strudel and Tyrolean pastries
food.desc: Paper-thin apple or curd strudel, Zillertaler Krapfen filled with grey cheese, and Strauben - funnel-fried batter with lingonberry jam at mountain huts.

places.name: Cafe Munding
places.note: Tyrol's oldest confectionery and cafe, in the same family since 1803; strudel, cakes and house chocolates.

places.name: Cafe Sacher Innsbruck
places.note: Opposite the Golden Roof for Sachertorte and strudel with whipped cream, in a proper coffee-house setting.

places.name: Markthalle Innsbruck
places.note: Market bakers sell strudel and Krapfen by the slice, far cheaper than the old-town cafes.

food.name: Tyrolean beer
food.desc: Unfiltered Zwickl and Marzen from Alpine breweries such as Zillertal, Starkenberger and the local Theresienbrau, poured half-litre with a thick head.

places.name: Theresienbrau
places.note: City-centre brewpub with copper kettles in the room; unfiltered house lager and hearty food until late.

places.name: Tribaun
places.note: Craft beer bar with a rotating Austrian tap list, popular with students and a younger crowd.

places.name: Stiftskeller
places.note: Big shaded beer garden in the heart of the old town, the easiest place for a first Tyrolean pint.

food.name: Schnaps and Zirbenlikor
food.desc: Clear fruit brandies distilled from Williams pear, plum or rowan, plus Zirben - a rose-coloured liqueur steeped from Alpine stone-pine cones.

places.name: Weisses Rossl
places.note: House schnapps offered after dinner, which is exactly how Tyroleans treat it.

places.name: Speckeria
places.note: Sells regional distillates and Zirbenschnaps alongside the Speck; good for tasting before buying.

places.name: Markthalle Innsbruck
places.note: Market stalls carry small-batch Tyrolean distillates and stone-pine liqueur from valley producers.

landmarks: Golden Roof (Goldenes Dachl)
Emperor Maximilian I's glittering balcony of 2,657 gilded copper tiles, the late-Gothic showpiece at the heart of Innsbruck's old town.
Nordkette Cable Car (Hafelekar)
A Zaha Hadid-designed funicular and cable-car chain whisking you from the city centre to 2,300-metre alpine ridges in under an hour.
Bergisel Ski Jump
Zaha Hadid's sleek tower crowning the Olympic ski jump, with a panoramic café gazing over Innsbruck and the Inn Valley.
Imperial Palace (Hofburg)
The Habsburgs' alpine residence, its rococo state rooms and Maria Theresa's grand apartments rivaling Vienna's imperial splendor in miniature.
Hofkirche (Court Church)
Home to Maximilian I's spectacular cenotaph, guarded by 28 larger-than-life bronze figures known as the Black Men.
Ambras Castle
A Renaissance hilltop castle housing Archduke Ferdinand II's celebrated chambers of art and curiosities, plus the dazzling Spanish Hall.
Maria-Theresien-Strasse and St. Anne's Column
Innsbruck's baroque boulevard, where pastel facades and the triumphal column frame the classic view toward the snowcapped Nordkette.
Innsbruck Cathedral (Dom St. Jakob)
A baroque jewel with lavish ceiling frescoes and Lucas Cranach's revered Madonna, tucked behind the Golden Roof.
City Tower (Stadtturm)
A 14th-century watchtower whose 133 steps deliver the definitive rooftop panorama of medieval lanes against the mountain wall.
Alpenzoo Innsbruck-Tirol
Europe's highest-altitude zoo, perched on the Nordkette slopes beside the 15th-century Weiherburg Castle, showcasing over 2,000 animals native to the Alps.

train.note: Innsbruck Hauptbahnhof is on the main east-west Alpine line: fast EuroCity and Railjet trains run to Munich in under two hours, to Zurich in about 3h30, and south through the Brenner to Verona. All are Schengen internal routes with no routine passport control.

bus.note: FlixBus coaches leave from the stop by Innsbruck Hauptbahnhof to Munich (about 2h30) and south over the Brenner Pass into Italy toward Verona; both cross Schengen internal borders with no routine passport control.

ferry.note: Innsbruck is a landlocked Alpine city on the upper Inn, which is not navigable here, so there are no ferries or scheduled boat services; the nearest passenger boats are the seasonal lake cruises on the Achensee, about an hour away.

half.blurb: Swarovski Kristallwelten (Crystal Worlds), a surreal art-and-crystal attraction with the Giant's head fountain and mirrored chambers.
half.name: Swarovski Crystal Worlds

half.blurb: A remarkably intact medieval salt-mining town on the Inn river with a walkable old centre, just 20 minutes east of Innsbruck.
half.name: Hall in Tirol

full.blurb: A year-round glacier ski and hiking area reached by cable car, topped by the Top of Tyrol viewing platform at over 3,200 m.
full.name: Stubai Glacier
